whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theDecidingReason: versioning-policy.v8 is 173 kB, it PASSED independent review, and IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE section 3 pins its digest as the VERSIONING head. A standalone successor would have to retype a reviewed contract to move a seven-character flag, and every retyped byte would leave the reviewed set without any instrument noticing. A derivation transcribes nothing: the reviewed surface is inherited by resolution, and the operation list is the complete and checkable statement of what left it.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theStructuralGuarantee: A derivation can only change what its operations name. The rules, custody classes, versioned identities, support windows, conformance tests, migrators, comparison fixtures and schemas are not named by any operation and therefore cannot be altered by this file. That is structural, not a promise.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.andItIsTheLINEAGEArgumentToo: v9 through v13 were standalone re-authors that carried the predecessor forward by transcription and then built machinery to prove the transcription was faithful. The machinery is what all NINE of their blocking findings are about - versioning-policy.v14 said eleven at this position and the recount is at $.inheritedMeasurementSweep.withdrawnInPlace. A derivation does not need that machinery, because it does not transcribe. The tenth blocking finding in this lineage, the one against v14, is the first that is not about machinery: it is about the navigation prose a derivation needs precisely BECAUSE it does not transcribe. That is the cost this shape carries, and this file pays it rather than trading it back for an apparatus.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.theCostAndWhyItIsPaid: The cost is that this file cannot be read as the document, and this corpus has paid that cost wrongly five times. It is paid here with the three mitigations the failing cases lacked - a first-key warning, a keyLocator that answers the exact question the failed greps were asking, and a reproducible digest of the resolved value - and with the repair the v14 review required of the second of them, because a mitigation that is wrong at one position is worse than none at that position.
whyADerivationAndNotAStandaloneDocument.whatWouldHaveMadeStandaloneRight: If the retention decision had invalidated the versioning contract's substance, a standalone re-author would be honest. It does not touch it. The decision falsifies exactly one leaf of this contract, and that leaf is a flag recording the state of another surface's decision.

resolutionAlgorithm.step1: Parse versioning-policy.v8.json with a duplicate-key-rejecting object_pairs_hook. Refuse on any duplicate.
resolutionAlgorithm.step2: Verify sha256(predecessor bytes) equals predecessorSha256. Refuse on mismatch.
resolutionAlgorithm.step3: Apply $.derivation.operations in array order to a deep copy.
resolutionAlgorithm.step4: For op 'set': navigate path, require the target to EXIST, and require its current value to be strictly equal to 'from'. Refuse otherwise.
resolutionAlgorithm.step5: For op 'add': navigate path, require the parent object to exist and the final key to be ABSENT. Refuse otherwise.
resolutionAlgorithm.step6: Refusal is total. A resolver that cannot satisfy every operation produces NO document; it never produces a partial one.
resolutionAlgorithm.pathGrammar: 'path' is an ARRAY of tokens: a JSON string is an object key, a JSON integer is a zero-based array index. There is no grammar to get wrong. 'pathDisplay' is a rendering for human readers and is NOT normative.
resolutionAlgorithm.strictEqualityRule: Strict equality is TYPE-EXACT and tests bool BEFORE int. In Python bool subclasses int, so True == 1 and isinstance(True, int) are both true; a 'from' guard written with == alone would accept an integer respelling of a boolean. versioning-policy.v9's own independent review measured exactly that hole in this lineage - 15 of 139 boolean leaves admitted an integer respelling at exit 0 - and this rule is written to be immune to it.
resolutionAlgorithm.keyOrder: Operations of kind 'add' append at the end of their parent object, so the resolved document's key order differs from the predecessor's. The canonical serialisation sorts keys, so the published digest is unaffected by order. No claim is made about any file's byte order.

theDecisionAsTheAuthorityRecordedIt.substance: Retention is bounded on time, size and count, all configurable per project, the three bounds independent by construction. A bound firing transitions the record to the existing PURGED state - degradation, not deletion: the record stays addressable, its recordCasRef is retained, effective capability never rises, and tombstones survive. A PURGED state carries a reason code. Default posture DURABLE_RETAINED with implicitDurableRetention YES: a project with no configured policy retains durably and unboundedly, and a durable-authoritative request with no policy PROCEEDS AND WRITES rather than refusing.
theDecisionAsTheAuthorityRecordedIt.override: The decision OVERRIDES retention-tiers.v22#recommendedDefaultPosture, whose own status was AWAITING-PRODUCT-DISPOSITION. whyV14AndNotV9ThroughV13.theFacts: v9, v10, v11, v12 and v13 all exist on disk. Each carries an independent review declaring CHANGES-REQUIRED with at least one finding of severity BLOCKING. Freeze section 2 rule 3 forbids implementing a rejected version and check-product-dispositions-v2.py's supersession derivation refuses to let a rejected successor displace anything, which is exactly why v8 is still the live head and still fails on the stale flag. Every verdict string, count and blocker title below was read from the review artifacts' own bytes for this successor, at the digests recorded; none is relayed from a summary.

blockers.title: The successor's own evidence block is 75% unenforced: the checker measures correctly, then does not compare the declaration against its measurement.

The enforcement discipline is NOT applied to v10's own new evidence block: 79 of its 316 positions are classified by a registry sized from the artifact, and the block's partition is measured, banner-printed and never compared. A false verdict-inheritance claim is admitted at exit 0.

The paper-seal class is declared CLOSED in free prose but is only PATTERN-closed. A verdict-inheritance claim worded differently from the reviewer's is admitted at exit 0 with the full green banner, including in top-level `role`.

A paper seal is planted at exit 0 by a ONE-FILE, ARTIFACT-ONLY edit with no checker edit. The closure is defined over the parsed JSON data model; the artifact of record is the FILE, and a duplicate key lives in the gap between them.

The live repoint rehearsal does not run the checker it says it runs. It measures a strict subset of the findings and reports a repair cost that is 3x to 4x below the measured on-disk cost, and reachedExitZero: true is false for both targets.

The O-05 repair substitutes the register only ONE level deep. A coordinator repoint therefore produces a VER12-PRED false positive that no artifact edit can repair, leaving the chain permanently red on the very act it is held pending.

THE BYTE GATE IS NOT OVER BYTES. It compares pathlib read_text(), which performs universal-newline translation, so a one-file artifact-only edit to the file's bytes is admitted at exit 0 while the banner asserts the file is byte-identical to the serialisation.

The repoint cost is wrong again. Declared v24 10 findings / 2 rounds / 11 leaf edits / exit 0 true; measured on disk 48 / 8 (round limit) / 41 / NO EXIT 0. The rehearsal cannot observe the two gates this successor is built on, and it holds its own rows fixed at the estimate it was given.

B-VER12R-03 is not closed, it is relocated. The register substitution reaches every module's load(), but the predecessor's DERIVED BUNDLE was already memoised under the live register, so after a real repoint the 'as recorded' arm compares against a repointed bundle and VER13-PRED and VER13-ATTR fire on pinned bytes no artifact edit can reach.

whyV14AndNotV9ThroughV13.whatTheFiveHaveInCommon: Not one of the eleven blocking findings is against the VERSIONING CONTRACT. Every one is against the self-evidence apparatus the successor bolted on to prove itself, or against the companion checker written to enforce that apparatus. The v9 review says so in its own words - it records the blocker 'against check-versioning-v9.py' and 'notAgainst versioning-policy.v9.json - no byte of the contract is wrong; every declaration I tested is TRUE' - and the v10 review reaches the same place from the other side.
whyV14AndNotV9ThroughV13.theTrajectory: The apparatus grew every time and the blockers grew with it. Read the titles above in order: a measurement that is never compared; a registry sized from the artifact it polices plus a partition printed in a banner and compared to nothing; a class declared closed in prose that is only pattern-closed; a closure defined over the parsed value while the artifact of record is the file; a byte gate that is not over bytes. The v13 review's own diagnosis of the lineage is that each time the boundary was drawn one layer above the bytes.
whyV14AndNotV9ThroughV13.whatV14DoesDifferently: It builds no self-evidence apparatus at all. There is no coverage census of this contract, no enforcement registry, no partition, no paper-seal scan, no repoint-cost rehearsal, no byte-identity claim and no companion checker. Every one of the eleven blockers is a finding about such an apparatus, and a document that has none is not reachable by any of them. This is a derived shape, not a chosen one: the reviews located the defect in the apparatus rather than in the contract five times running, so the apparatus is what this successor omits.
whyV14AndNotV9ThroughV13.theOnlyNumbersThisFilePublishesAboutItse: The operation count and the two op-kind counts in $.operationAccounting, and a leaf census of the RESOLVED value in $.resolvedValue. Nothing here prints a figure that nothing can be compared against, which is the shape of B-VER9R-01 and B-VER10R-01.

inheritedMeasurementSweep.whyThisBlockExists: Freeze section 7.3’s rider of 2026-08-05: a derivation TRANSCRIBES nothing but INHERITS everything, and inherited MEASUREMENTS go stale under the successor’s name. Resolution republishes every predecessor field the delta does not touch under this file’s name and date, and a measurement that ages that way ages silently, because nothing in the delta mentions it and a reader sees only the successor’s signature against it. The rule the rider states is that a derivation must say, for every inherited measurement, either that it re-measured it or that it did not. This block says it for all of them.
inheritedMeasurementSweep.whatCountsAsInheritedHere: Two things. Second, the measurements the resolution itself inherits from versioning-policy.v8.json. Byte-identity with the predecessor is NOT a defence: that is precisely the condition under which a stale figure survives.

NAME COLLISION. artifacts/check-versioning-v14.py IS NOT THIS FILE’S CHECKER AND NOT versioning-policy.v14’S. Everywhere else in this corpus check-versioning-vN.py validates versioning-policy.vN.json; this one declares BINDING = "versioning-policy.v8.json" at line 159 and carries a NAME COLLISION HAZARD section at line 121 saying so. Two lanes chose the number 14 for unrelated things. A reader applying the corpus convention reaches for the wrong instrument, in the direction that reads as validation where there is none. It is pinned in this file, unlike in v14, because it is no longer under active authorship and statements made about it depend on its bytes.

The lineage account quotes each review’s declared verdict string, counts and blocker titles verbatim from its bytes. It does NOT re-run any of the experiments those reviews performed, and it takes each review’s own measurements on trust - except the blocker COUNT, which this lane recomputed and found wrong. See $.inheritedMeasurementSweep.withdrawnInPlace.

The claim that no blocking finding in the five is against the versioning contract rests on reading the blockers’ declared "against" and "notAgainst" fields and their titles. It is a reading of the reviews, not an independent adjudication of them.

The resolved-value digest binds a canonical serialisation of a parsed value. It says nothing about any file’s bytes, and it cannot detect a resolver that parses the predecessor with a duplicate key admitted - which is why step 1 of the resolution algorithm is the hook and not the digest.
This file’s own top-level structure is not validated by anything.

THE REPAIR IS PROSE, AND PROSE IS WHAT WENT WRONG. The keyLocator is a hand-maintained map. Nothing in this corpus recomputes it, nothing fails if it drifts, and the collision set published at $.topLevelNameCollisions is a measurement taken once at authoring. The v14 review’s fourth remedy suggested deriving the set rather than writing it; deriving it would require a companion checker, and a companion checker is what every one of the nine blocking findings against v9 through v13 is about. This file chose the smaller exposure and names it here rather than claiming the class is closed.
